---
title: "minitable"
---





`minitable` provides a few `tibble`-style construction/coercion
helpers -- `mtable_tibble()`, `mtable_as_tibble()`,
`mtable_rownames_to_column()`, `mtable_add_row()` -- built entirely on
`data.frame()`/`as.data.frame()`. Results are plain data frames, not
tibbles. See the
[README](https://github.com/djnavarro/minis/tree/main/minitable) for
the full scope notes; this page walks through each function, including
the cross-column-reference behaviour that took real rework to get
right (see `.agents/HISTORY.md` in the repository for the bug that
surfaced along the way).

## `mtable_tibble()`: sequential, cross-referencing construction

Like `tibble::tibble()`, later columns can refer to earlier ones by
name -- each column is evaluated in order, in an environment built
from the columns already constructed:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtable_tibble(a = 1:3, b = a * 2, c = a + b)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  a b c
1 1 2 3
2 2 4 6
3 3 6 9
```


:::
:::



This only works because the sequential-evaluation logic lives directly
inside `mtable_tibble()` itself, rather than in a shared helper that
`...` gets forwarded through -- forwarding `...` turns each argument
into an opaque `..1`/`..2` pronoun that resolves free variables against
the *caller's* environment instead of the custom one being built up
column by column, silently breaking exactly this feature.

## Unnamed arguments are named after their deparsed expression

Just as in `tibble::tibble()`, an argument with no `name =` is named
after its own source expression:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtable_tibble(1:3, sqrt(1:3))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  1:3 sqrt(1:3)
1   1  1.000000
2   2  1.414214
3   3  1.732051
```


:::
:::



## `mtable_as_tibble()`: coercion only

There's no tibble class or special printing here -- it's just
`as.data.frame()` with `check.names = FALSE` (so literal, non-syntactic
column names survive):



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtable_as_tibble(list(a = 1:2, b = c("x", "y")))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  a b
1 1 x
2 2 y
```


:::
:::



## `mtable_rownames_to_column()`: no-op on default row names

A data frame with only the default sequential row names (`"1"`, `"2"`,
...) is returned unchanged -- there's nothing meaningful to move into
a column:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
identical(
  mtable_rownames_to_column(data.frame(x = 1:3), var = "id"),
  data.frame(x = 1:3)
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] TRUE
```


:::
:::



Real (non-default) row names do get moved into a new column:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtable_rownames_to_column(head(mtcars, 3), var = "model")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
          model  mpg cyl disp  hp drat    wt  qsec vs am gear carb
1     Mazda RX4 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.620 16.46  0  1    4    4
2 Mazda RX4 Wag 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.875 17.02  0  1    4    4
3    Datsun 710 22.8   4  108  93 3.85 2.320 18.61  1  1    4    1
```


:::
:::



## `mtable_add_row()`: the same cross-referencing support

Appending a row supports the same sequential evaluation as
`mtable_tibble()`, so a later value in the new row can refer to an
earlier one:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
df <- mtable_tibble(a = 1:2, b = a * 10)
mtable_add_row(df, a = 3, b = a * 10)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
  a  b
1 1 10
2 2 20
3 3 30
```


:::
:::
